newsitem.title: USA: Goldman Sachs says 1996 its second best year.
newsitem.headline: Goldman Sachs says 1996 its second best year.

text.p: Goldman Sachs & Co. said Tuesday that 1996 was the second best year in the investment bank's history, with pretax profits jumping to $2.6 billion from $1.37 billion in fiscal 1995.
The firm's best year was in 1993, when it earned $2.7 billion.
Boosted by the strength in financial markets, the investment bank said revenues for the year jumped 37 percent to $6.14 billion from $4.48 billion.
Expenses were $3.53 billion for the year compared to $3.11 billion last year and headcount was near 9,000 compared to 8,200 employees in 1995. Capital is now about $5.25 billion, the firm said.

"It's not surprising they did so well, just about everything they participate in had good results for the year as a whole," said independent analyst Perrin Long, citing strong mergers and acquisition activity as well as strength in fixed-income securities.
The fourth quarter was the firm's third best quarter ever, Goldman said.

For the fourth quarter, the firm earned $743 million on a pretax basis, up 68 percent from the $440 million earned last year. Revenues for the quarter were $1.54 billion compared to $1.3 billion last year and expenses were $790 million compared to $860 million last year.

In a statement, Goldman Chief Financial Officer John Thain said, "Fourth quarter performance was very strong with all divisions contributing across the board to profitable results for the quarter and for the year."

Long said because Goldman's fiscal year ended on Nov. 30, its annual profits might look better than other Wall Street firms, because other firms would have to include December, when the market was not as strong overall, in their 1996 results.
"It will be a real test for them in 1997 to match 1996 earnings -- 1997 hasn't gotten off to a very rousing start," Long said.
